The discussions during this workshop reinforced the importance of balancing innovation with worker protection, promoting human oversight, and ensuring transparency and accountability in workplace AI applications.  The workshop also highlighted the importance of practical, workplace-based learning. We will continue to explore how vocational training and public employment services can better support workers and MSMEs in adopting AI through hands-on learning and practical applications, rather than focusing only on AI literacy.
Potential Barriers: One challenge is that AI technologies are evolving much faster than policy development. Governments need time to consult stakeholders and develop practical guidance, while AI applications continue to change rapidly. Therefore, continued collaboration among government, employers, workers, technology providers, and training institutions will be essential to translate these ideas into practical actions.

The discussions during this workshop reinforced the importance of balancing innovation with worker protection, promoting human oversight, and ensuring transparency and accountability in workplace AI applications. We will continue to explore how vocational training and public employment services can better support workers and MSMEs in adopting AI through hands-on learning and practical applications, rather than focusing only on AI literacy.
Potential Barriers: One challenge is that AI technologies are evolving much faster than policy development. Therefore, continued collaboration among government, employers, workers, technology providers, and training institutions will be essential to translate these ideas into practical actions.
